channel.title: Exploring Electronics
channel.description: Electronics from first principles — voltage, current, resistance, and circuit design explained clearly. Real components, real numbers, no prior knowledge assumed.

item.title: Soldering
item.description: How soldering works: solder bonds only to clean, hot metal. Heating the parts, flux, choosing solder and temperature, judging a joint, desoldering, and fume and lead safety.

item.title: Bench Power Supplies
item.description: How a bench power supply works: an adjustable regulator with a current limit. CV and CC modes, the crossover, a safe first power-up, and reading the spec sheet.

item.title: SPI
item.description: How SPI works: two shift registers swapping bits on every clock, a chip-select wire instead of an address, clock modes, and reading an MCP3008 ADC from an Arduino.

item.title: Overview
item.description: The Communication articles in reading order: serial between two devices, the I²C bus for many sensors on two wires, and fast SPI with a wire per device.

item.title: I²C
item.description: How the I²C bus lets an Arduino talk to many sensors on two wires: open-drain lines and pull-ups, a shared clock, 7-bit addresses, ACK, and reading an MCP9808.

item.title: Serial Communication
item.description: How serial (UART) works: one bit at a time on one wire, no clock, just an agreed baud rate. Framing, wiring TX to RX, voltage levels, and two-way Arduino serial.

item.title: Overview
item.description: The Power articles in reading order: cells and batteries, then voltage regulators and the power supplies that turn a wall outlet into steady DC.

item.title: Voltage Regulators
item.description: How a voltage regulator holds a steady output: linear regulators and their heat, dropout, switching regulators, and the stages of a complete power supply.

item.title: Vacuum Tubes
item.description: How a vacuum tube works: a heated cathode, a positive plate, and a grid that controls the stream. Diodes and triodes, why tubes resemble FETs, and why they're still made.

item.title: Using a Multimeter
item.description: How a multimeter works: why the jacks matter more than the dial, what the fuse and CAT rating protect, auto-ranging and accuracy, and the habits that keep readings honest.

item.title: Voltage Dividers
item.description: How two resistors split a voltage, why the output collapses under load, and how to scale a 12 V battery down for an Arduino's analog pin safely.

item.title: Overview
item.description: The fourteen Circuit Foundations articles in reading order: charge, voltage, current, resistance, Ohm's law, AC, magnetism, capacitors, and inductors, with real numbers.

item.title: Overview
item.description: The Components articles in reading order: resistors, diodes and LEDs, transistors, vacuum tubes, temperature sensors, and the physical packages parts come in.

item.title: Overview
item.description: The Microcontrollers articles in reading order: the Arduino board and its code, digital pins, blinking an LED, reading buttons and analog sensors, and staged output.

item.title: Overview
item.description: The bench equipment this site uses: breadboards, arduino-cli for programming an Arduino, the multimeter, the bench power supply, and soldering.

item.title: Inductors
item.description: How an inductor stores energy in a magnetic field and resists any change in current: the henry, what sets a coil's inductance, the L/R time constant, and why switching one off bites.

item.title: Transistors
item.description: How a transistor lets a tiny current or voltage control a large one: bipolar and field-effect transistors, switching a 12 V load from an Arduino pin, and amplifying.

item.title: Diodes and LEDs
item.description: How a diode lets current through one way only, why every LED colour has its own forward voltage, how to size an LED resistor properly, and what diodes do in real circuits.

item.title: Capacitors
item.description: How a capacitor stores charge between two plates, what a farad is, why it fills on an RC curve, and how a camera flash turns two AA cells into a 15 kW burst.

item.title: Resistor Types
item.description: What's inside carbon, metal-film, and wire-wound resistors, what a temperature coefficient means, and how potentiometers, rheostats, trimmers, and tapped resistors work.
